correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization gives an exact product decomposition of the t-Krylov module; primitive idempotents prove the free-module criterion; classical slice grades determine the first noninvertible tubal subdiagonal; componentwise pseudoinversion gives exact support normalization and projective continuation. The explicit real and positive-tolerance families were reproduced numerically.

originality.rationale: Prior tensor-Arnoldi work already defines noninvertible-tubal-scalar breakdown and simultaneous Fourier-slice Arnoldi, and classical block Krylov work already uses deflation. The inspected sources did not state the minimum-grade breakdown theorem, non-free module mechanism, support-idempotent continuation to the maximum grade, or the positive-tolerance premature-stop family. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The obstruction can stop a tensor-function Arnoldi calculation while other Fourier slices remain arbitrarily far from their Krylov grades. The support-deflated formulation separates local from global convergence, gives exact recovery at the maximum grade, and can avoid padded frontal matrix-vector products.
